_meta.title: Analysis & Synthesis Methods — dataset for the Design Methods Map
_meta.purpose: Content for the analysis section: the methods students use to turn collected data into findings.
_meta.audience: Beginner-first. The 'level' field drives the beginner-friendly UI; the portal should hide Advanced methods behind an off-by-default 'Show advanced methods' toggle and badge any Advanced method that is shown.

schemaFields.name: Display name.
schemaFields.dataType: Reuses the portal's existing vocabulary: Qualitative, Quantitative, Behavioral, Attitudinal.
schemaFields.outputType: What the method produces. One of the controlled values in outputTypeVocabulary.
schemaFields.inputMethods: Slug ids of COLLECTION methods this analysis is applied to (see inputMethodReconciliation).
schemaFields.phase: Lifecycle stage(s), reusing the portal's five-stage vocabulary.
schemaFields.rigourNote: How to do it defensibly — surfaced in the method detail view.

_meta.inputMethodReconciliation: The 'inputMethods' values are slug placeholders referencing COLLECTION methods already in the portal. Before use, reconcile each against the real collection-method ids (Phase 0/1 of the brief). Remap or remove any that do not resolve so every link is valid in both directions.
_meta.referencingStyle: Short author-year (APA 7). Expand to a full bibliography separately if required.

analysisMethods.name: Affinity Diagramming (KJ Method)
analysisMethods.blurb: Cluster individual observations or quotes into emergent groups to surface shared themes from messy qualitative notes.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Build clusters bottom-up from the data rather than sorting into pre-decided buckets; name each cluster only after grouping.

analysisMethods.name: Thematic Analysis
analysisMethods.blurb: Systematically code qualitative data and develop, review and name themes that answer the research question.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: State whether coding is inductive (data-driven) or deductive (theory-driven); keep a codebook and an audit trail.

analysisMethods.name: Journey / Experience Mapping
analysisMethods.blurb: Plot a user's actions, thoughts and emotions across the stages of an experience to expose pain points and opportunities.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Ground every stage and emotion in evidence from your data; mark assumptions clearly where evidence is thin.

analysisMethods.name: Persona Synthesis
analysisMethods.blurb: Consolidate patterns across users into a small set of representative archetypes to guide design decisions.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Derive personas from observed behavioural patterns, not demographics alone; avoid inventing traits unsupported by data.

analysisMethods.name: Descriptive Statistics
analysisMethods.blurb: Summarise numeric data with counts, means, medians, spread and simple charts to describe what was observed.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Choose summaries that match the measurement scale (for example, the median for ordinal data) and always report the sample size.

analysisMethods.name: Qualitative Content Analysis
analysisMethods.blurb: Categorise text into a coding scheme and, where useful, count category frequencies to compare across cases.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Define categories before counting and assess inter-coder reliability (for example, Cohen's kappa) when more than one coder is involved.

analysisMethods.name: Framework Analysis
analysisMethods.blurb: Chart coded qualitative data into a matrix of themes by case to compare systematically across participants.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Keep the framework matrix transparent so readers can trace each summary cell back to its source quotes.

analysisMethods.name: Inferential Tests (t-test, ANOVA, chi-square, correlation, regression)
analysisMethods.blurb: Test whether differences or relationships seen in your sample are likely to hold in the wider population.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Match the test to your data type and design, check assumptions, and report effect sizes and confidence intervals, not just p-values.

analysisMethods.name: Reliability Analysis (Cronbach's α, McDonald's ω)
analysisMethods.blurb: Check how consistently a set of survey items measures the same underlying construct.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Report which coefficient you used and why; alpha assumes items contribute equally, so prefer omega when that does not hold.

analysisMethods.name: Triangulation (Joint Displays)
analysisMethods.blurb: Integrate qualitative and quantitative findings to corroborate, complement or explain results from a single source.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Use a joint display to set qualitative and quantitative evidence side by side and state explicitly where they agree or diverge.

analysisMethods.name: Grounded-Theory Coding (open, axial, selective)
analysisMethods.blurb: Build a theory directly from data through successive coding stages, comparing cases until categories are saturated.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Use constant comparison and theoretical sampling; keep analytic memos so the emerging theory is traceable to the data.

analysisMethods.name: Exploratory Factor Analysis / PCA
analysisMethods.blurb: Reduce many correlated survey items to a smaller set of underlying factors or components.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Check sampling adequacy (KMO, Bartlett's test), justify the number of factors retained, and report the rotation used.

analysisMethods.name: Mokken Scale Analysis
analysisMethods.blurb: A non-parametric item-response approach that tests whether items form a hierarchical, unidimensional scale.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Report scalability coefficients (H), assess monotonicity and invariant item ordering, and justify the scaling threshold used.

analysisMethods.name: Rasch Analysis
analysisMethods.blurb: A probabilistic item-response model that places persons and items on the same interval scale to test measurement quality.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Examine item and person fit statistics and report whether the data fit the model, rather than adjusting the model to the data.

analysisMethods.name: Cluster Analysis
analysisMethods.blurb: Group respondents into segments with similar response patterns to reveal natural user types.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Standardise variables before clustering, justify the number of clusters, and validate stability on a holdout or an alternative method.

analysisMethods.name: Conjoint Analysis / MaxDiff
analysisMethods.blurb: Estimate the relative importance of features or attributes from the trade-offs respondents make between options.
analysisMethods.rigourNote: Design the choice tasks to be balanced and realistic, and report attribute utilities or importance scores with their uncertainty.
